title: Seville or Málaga in winter: which is better for a break?
author: Matt
intro: In winter, Málaga is a little warmer and has the sea, more flights and a beach to walk on, while Seville has the bigger sights and the more festive old town. Both are about 16 to 18°C by day. Here's how they compare from November to February.
seo_title: Seville or Málaga in winter? Málaga is milder (2026)
seo_description: Málaga is slightly warmer in winter, with the sea and more flights. Seville has bigger sights and colder nights. Both are 16-18°C by day. Compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warmer:** Málaga, by a degree or two
- **Bigger sights:** Seville
- **Beach walks:** Málaga
- **Both:** about 2 hrs apart by train

They're both good winter city breaks, mild and sunny when the UK is grey. Choose Málaga for a relaxed break by the sea with easy flights, and Seville if the Alcázar, the cathedral and the old town are what you're going for.

sections.heading: Seville and Málaga compared
sections.text:
| | Seville | Málaga |
| --- | --- | --- |
| December high | about 17°C | about 18°C |
| January high | about 16°C | about 17°C |
| February high | about 18°C | about 18°C |
| Nights | colder, inland | milder, by the sea |
| Flights from the UK | fewer routes | lots, from most UK airports |
| Best for | monuments, old town, flamenco | sea, food, museums, day trips |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Seville](/destinations/seville) and [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) guides. Seville is inland, so although its days are similar, its winter nights are noticeably colder than Málaga's by the sea.

sections.heading: Seville in winter
sections.text:
Winter is one of the best times to see Seville. In summer it's one of the hottest cities in Europe, but from November to February you can walk all day in comfort, and the orange trees that line the streets are full of fruit.

- **The Real Alcázar:** the royal palace and gardens, best booked ahead for a timed entry.
- **The cathedral and the Giralda:** one of the world's largest Gothic cathedrals, with a ramp up the old minaret tower.
- **Plaza de España:** the huge tiled semicircle in María Luisa Park.
- **Flamenco:** small, intimate shows in Triana and the Santa Cruz quarter.

At Christmas, the city fills with nativity scenes, known as belenes, in churches and markets. Our [Seville in 3 days](/blog/seville-in-3-days) post plans a short break.

sections.heading: Málaga in winter
sections.text:
Málaga is a city break and a seaside break in one. You can spend the morning in the Picasso Museum or up at the Alcazaba fortress, and the afternoon walking along the beach at La Malagueta.

- **The Alcazaba and Gibralfaro:** a Moorish fortress and castle above the city, with views over the port.
- **Museums:** the Picasso Museum, the Centre Pompidou Málaga and the Carmen Thyssen.
- **Food:** tapas in the old town, and fried fish and espetos, sardines grilled on the beach.
- **Day trips:** [Ronda](/destinations/ronda), [Nerja](/destinations/nerja) and [Granada](/destinations/granada) are all within reach.

Local knowledge: Calle Larios, Málaga's main shopping street, is famous for its Christmas lights, which usually go up from late November with a light and music show in the evenings.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
Málaga is one of the easiest Spanish airports to reach from the UK, with direct flights from most UK airports all year, usually about 2¾ hours. The airport is close to the city, with a fast train to the centre.

Seville has fewer UK routes, mostly from London and a few regional airports, with flights of about 2¾ hours too. If there's no direct flight from your airport, fly to Málaga and take the train: high-speed services between the two cities take about 2 hours.

Watch out: in Seville, many sights have shorter hours on Mondays or close on some public holidays, including 25 December, 1 January and 6 January. Check before you plan your days.

sections.heading: Christmas and Three Kings
sections.text:
Both cities make a lot of the festive season, and it runs later than at home. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day are family days, but the big street event is the Three Kings parade (Cabalgata de Reyes) on the evening of 5 January, with floats throwing sweets to the crowds.

- **Seville:** nativity scenes (belenes) in churches and shop windows, and a Christmas craft market near the cathedral in December. The old town is lovely on a cold, clear evening.
- **Málaga:** the Calle Larios lights usually go up in late November, with a light and music show several times each evening. Check this year's times before you go.
- **Both:** shops and some sights close or shorten their hours on 25 December, 1 January and 6 January, so plan museum visits around those days.

If you want quieter streets and lower prices, mid-January to February is the sweet spot in both cities, once the Christmas crowds have gone home.

sections.heading: Which to choose
sections.text:
- **For a first trip to Andalusia:** Seville, for the Alcázar and the old town.
- **For a relaxed winter break with the sea:** Málaga.
- **For the most flight choice:** Málaga.
- **For four nights or more:** both, with two nights in each and the train in between.

For more of the region, see [Granada](/destinations/granada) and [Córdoba](/destinations/cordoba), or the [holidays in Spain](/destinations/holidays-in-spain) page. If you still can't decide, add both to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: Is Seville or Málaga warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: Málaga, slightly. Both are about 16 to 18°C by day, but Málaga's nights are milder because it's on the coast.

faqs.question: Is Seville worth visiting in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes. Winter is cool and comfortable for sightseeing, the queues are shorter than in spring, and the orange trees are in fruit.

faqs.question: How far is Seville from Málaga?
faqs.answer: About 2 hours by high-speed train, or a little longer by car or coach.

faqs.question: Can you go to the beach in Málaga in winter?
faqs.answer: You can walk on the beach and sit in the sun on many days, but the sea is cool, so it's not really swimming weather for most people.
